text:
Priya R: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing to extract tenant affinity (sticky routing / 'affinity tokens') out of session-mesh into a small affinity-service. RFC link: https://redwood.internal/rfc/affinity-demux (summary below).

Mike L: session-mesh already does this. Why split?

Priya R: Mainly to reduce hot-path complexity in session-mesh, share affinity logic across runtimes (hosted, dedicated, private), and let us iterate caching/eviction independently.

Sasha: Adding a hop worries me for p50. Do we have perf numbers?

Priya R: Prototype shows local sidecar adds ~350us median. With local cache hits, no remote call. Synthetic token-path p50 changed by ~1%. We can also offer in-process lib for low-latency runtimes.

Andre: What does the API look like?

Priya R: Minimal: GET /v1/affinity?tenant_id=acme-1&trace_id=... returns token+node+expiry. Example response body: {"token":"ABCD..","node":"node-42","expires_at":"1680000000"}. Runtimes can also call affinity.lookup(tenant,key) via local lib.

Leah: Where is the state stored? Durable?

Priya R: Three tiers: local LRU cache in sidecars, regional Raft-replicated delta store for active sets, optional Postgres for cold state. Active sets are small so Raft per-region is reasonable.

Mike L: Migration plan? We have long-lived sessions we can't break.

Priya R: Migration steps: 1) Deploy affinity-service and run session-mesh in read-only shadow mode (session-mesh queries new service but keeps writes). 2) Shadow for 2 weeks, assert token parity >99.99%. 3) Flip session-mesh to read-write with canary header X-Affinity-Source: affinity-service for 10% tenants. Monitor. 4) Full cutover and remove old code.

Sasha: Cache consistency edge cases — stale token leading to wrong routing?

Priya R: Use generation numbers in tokens and short TTLs (30s default). On mismatch router falls back to deterministic hashing and we emit affinity.divergence.count. Reconciliation job runs every 15m.

Andre: Rollback?

Priya R: Feature flags in session-mesh let us route reads back to session-mesh and stop writes. Runbook available in RFC.

Leah: What metrics and SLOs?

Priya R: affinity.latency.p50/p95, affinity.error_rate, affinity.cache_hit_ratio, affinity.token_mismatch_rate, routing.fallback_rate. Dashboard with canary tenant annotations.

Mike L: Security of tokens in headers? Forgery risk?

Priya R: Tokens are HMAC-signed with short TTLs, no PII. Private deployments can bring their KMS.

Sasha: Testing plan? Chaos tests?

Priya R: Yes: unit, integration, pod-kill, network partition, raft leader stepdown, load tests with Zipf tenant skew.

Andre: Ownership?

Priya R: Eng-Runtime owns for 6 months, then rotate to Platform if broadly used. Quarterly review.

Leah: On-prem deploy surface?

Priya R: Two modes: embedded library for on-prem runtime or standalone service (K8s+helm).

deploy-bot: Deployed prototype to staging: affinity-service:v0.1. Canary set 'alpha' created.

Mike L: +1, add perf budget and ensure deterministic hash fallback without config changes.

Sasha: +1, also add token audit to privacy review.

Andre: +1, add migration postmortem checklist to epic.

Priya R: I'll open the tracking epic with infra/helm, Raft spike, sidecar integration, session-mesh shadow PR, e2e tests, dashboard/alerts. Planning to start spike tomorrow unless blockers. Will ping #eng-release.
